daily.basis: UTC day of first_seen over the whole bank; a day with no mined row is absent, not zero; raw volume is reported beside the independent counts so a fall in duplicates can never hide a fall in mining
daily.rule: new_independent_cells = first cell of an L1 rule never mined before; new_independent_families = first cell of an L2 family; duplicate_share = 1 - new_independent_cells / raw_cells

intake.rule: a duplicate is KEPT and a re-aimed descendant is minted beside it; nothing is deleted, so the mint rate can only rise. Once per parent, ever: reaim_ledger.jsonl OR a child already in the docket

inheritance.rule: an EXACT twin (same executable identity) inherits any verdict -- it is the same test. A non-identical member of an L1 rule or L2 family inherits ONLY a REJECT at a family-invariant gate (economic_prior, only between members with the same mechanism_status, which is all that gate reads) or, on the SAME instrument, at an instrument-invariant gate (symbol_eligibility). A PASS is never inherited, nor any reject at a parameter-dependent gate (in_sample_screen, deflated_sharpe, cpcv, walk_forward, lockbox, stress_costs, swap_cost, pbo, spa): those members are judged, after the representative. Every inheritor stays in the trial count exactly as if judged.
inheritance.why: the sealed gauntlet decides what it judges; inheritance there is a proposal patch (patches/judge_families) that charges every inheritor to the effective-trial census as if judged

trial_count.why: this organ reorders and re-aims; it never removes a row, skips a judgement or writes a trial ledger, so N is exactly what the sealed lifetime union already counts
